briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Tops $17B in Sales as Tax Relief Gains Steam; Feds Clear Path on Rescheduling and Psychedelics
briefs.top: Michigan's legal market just crossed $17 billion in lifetime sales even as operators push hard for wholesale-tax relief — with a repeal bill in Lansing and a gubernatorial candidate courting industry cash. Nationally, courts just upheld federal marijuana rescheduling and the FDA is fast-tracking psychedelic therapies, while MSOs jockey for position through a wave of acquisitions.

local.text: Michigan cannabis sales cross $17 billion milestone
local.detail: The state has now surpassed $17 billion in combined adult-use and medical marijuana sales since legalization, generating an estimated $2.66 billion in state excise and sales taxes, per a new CRA report.
local.text_full: Michigan cannabis sales cross $17 billion milestone — the state has now surpassed $17 billion in combined adult-use and medical marijuana sales since legalization, generating an estimated $2.66 billion in state excise and sales taxes, per a new CRA report.

local.text: John James courts cannabis donors with tax-repeal vow — Michigan's GOP gubernatorial nominee is promising to repeal or sharply reduce the 24% wholesale tax, and a JARS Cannabis-hosted fundraiser alone netted his campaign nearly $90,000.

JARS Cannabis buys its way into Arizona — the Michigan-based chain is acquiring Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa dispensaries, a deal that will make JARS the largest dispensary operator in Arizona.

Grön's Pearls gummies land on Michigan shelves — the Wyld-owned edibles brand rolled its bestselling Pearls gummies into Michigan as part of a four-state expansion, already stocked at Pure Options, High Profile and Lume.
Wholesale tax underperforms, fueling repeal momentum — the 24% tax brought in only about $34-37 million a quarter versus a $105 million projection, adding fuel to a new House repeal bill, HB 6224.

national.text: Court upholds federal marijuana rescheduling to Schedule III — the D.C. Circuit rejected a challenge to the medical marijuana rescheduling order, keeping the historic Schedule III shift intact as the DEA weighs full rescheduling.

FDA holds landmark hearing on psychedelic therapies — regulators gathered expert input on clinical pathways for psilocybin and methylone-based treatments, with Compass Pathways' COMP360 eyeing a possible late-2026 approval milestone.

Eli Lilly closes its AtaiBeckley psychedelics acquisition — the pharma giant's deal, approved by stockholders and expected to close mid-September, brings psychedelic assets BPL-003, VLS-01 and EMP-01 under Lilly's development umbrella.
Cresco Labs completes $50M Pennsylvania dispensary buy — the MSO closed its acquisition of nine Pennsylvania medical marijuana dispensaries, expanding its East Coast retail footprint.

Curaleaf-Aurora takeover fight signals consolidation wave — Aurora's board is urging shareholders to reject Curaleaf's hostile bid, calling it undervalued, as the MSO sector's biggest fight for scale plays out in real time.
